summary: The complete 95-page exactPDF221B presents credible finite lattice estimates, rank obstructions, signed-penalty examples and adaptive geometric bounds. The new coefficient-selected unit shell and matching off-center-hole loss are meaningful local additions. I found no principal-theorem contradiction under the stated hypotheses. Minor revision is warranted for a specific Brudnyi Appendix I scope qualification and clearer contribution/dependency mapping. Classical ingredients are substantial, exact priority remains uncertain, and neither the unrestricted rectangle adapter nor a physical continuum result is established. This is a first declared assessment of B with retained prior participation disclosed, not independent human peer review.
strengths: Exact rank-nullity and low-frequency constructions distinguish coarse information from coercivity without hiding volume dependence.
Singular Schur and signed-penalty examples retain the kernel cross-term condition and identify failures of kernel-only reasoning.
Critical-moment and finite Sobolev arguments track lattice normalization, reflection multiplicity, thin geometry and admissible coefficient classes.
Section 40.1 selects a unit shell from the original critical moment and obtains bounded face rank with the correct scale.
Sections 40.2–40.3 distinguish failed internal or punctured-domain certificates from successful full-energy bounds and provide matching orders.
weaknesses: The global coefficient-selected rectangle adapter remains open; the new shell lemma supplies no complete global rank and covering accounting.
Priority of the exact refinements is not established by the targeted primary-source checks, while the main methods have extensive classical antecedents.
The 95-page accumulation of examples and provenance narrative obscures the hierarchy of new theorems and their dependencies.
Formal endpoints, source build claims and selected finite runs have not been replayed in this assessment and do not certify the full manuscript.
potential_errors: Page 92 describes Brudnyi Appendix I through a strictly interior dyadic cube, but Remark I.2 also covers boundary-touching dyadic inner cubes. Qualify this description and distinguish dyadic geometry from the weighted-energy adapter; no current principal theorem is thereby refuted.
Extending scalar axis tents or off-center Neumann-domain examples to coexact or divergence-constrained fields would require additional proof; that extension was not established here.
Interpreting route-specific internal-energy or punctured-domain failures as an unrestricted full-cube rectangle impossibility would exceed the proved quantifiers.
